name: logfire
readme_html:
Logfire for Kedi

Configure Pydantic AI model/tool tracing from a Kedi program, with optional HTTPX request spans. No instrumentation runs until configure_logfire is called.

Install

kedi add logfire

Kedi installs the manifest's logfire[httpx] dependency into the Python interpreter running the command. Use a Kedi client with automatic python_dependencies installation; older clients require python -m pip install 'logfire[httpx]>=4.41,<5' in the same environment.

For a local checkout, run kedi install library/logfire/package.kedi from the registry repository root instead.

Use

> import: logfire

`configure_logfire("city-guide")`

> model: openai:gpt-5.6-luna
>> The capital of Sweden is [city: str].
> show: The selected city is <city>.

`flush_logfire()`

Set LOGFIRE_TOKEN or authenticate using the Python Logfire CLI to send data to a project. Without a token the program still runs and Logfire can display local console output. Tokens belong in the environment, never in .kedi source.

API

configure_logfire(service_name="kedi", capture_content=False, httpx=False) configures the process-wide Logfire SDK and Pydantic AI instrumentation. In native Kedi calls, pass options positionally:

> import: logfire

`configure_logfire("city-guide", False, True)`

The third argument enables HTTPX spans; request/response bodies and headers are not captured. The second argument opts into model content capture. Configure once during startup, before model calls. Importing this package does not select a model or expose tools to an agent.

flush_logfire() returns a boolean indicating whether pending telemetry was flushed within three seconds. Call it when finishing a short-lived program.

This package instruments Pydantic AI and optionally HTTPX. Full Kedi runtime, artifact, and workflow instrumentation is provided separately by opentelemetry-instrumentation-kedi. When that instrumentor owns Pydantic AI instrumentation, configure Logfire directly rather than enabling that same integration a second time through this package.
